answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and stands that color's Player ID card visibly in front of them. Give each player the Voting set with the same color on its backs, remove cards targeting colors not in play, and keep each player's own Ambush. Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center with values hidden; the deck remains face down beside the play area.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'stands its Player ID card visibly in front of them'; 'Remove cards targeting colors that are not playing'; 'Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center'.

answers.answer: There is no player-by-player turn order. A player may change their face-down card until cards are revealed. Once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'There is no individual turn order.' Vote: 'You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed' and 'reveal all choices simultaneously.'

answers.answer: No. A four-vote majority is not required. Red is the Target because Red has the most votes; the player or players with the most votes are Targets, including when the most-voted total is tied.
answers.evidence: Vote: 'The player receiving the most votes is the Target. If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets.'

answers.answer: With neither protected by a successful Ambush, both Red and Blue are eliminated as tied Targets. A player who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and may survive, subject to the successful Ambush rule.
answers.evidence: Vote: tied players 'are Targets'; 'Each Target is eliminated unless protected by its own successful Ambush'; with tied Targets, 'voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.'

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated: every player who did not vote for any Target is eliminated, unless protected by the successful Ambush exception. Green voted for Red, not the sole Target Blue, and did not Ambush.
answers.evidence: Vote: 'Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated, subject to the successful Ambush exception.'

answers.answer: Red's Ambush does not count as a vote. From the stated votes, Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow produce a one-to-one tie, so Red and Yellow are the Targets. Red is a Target, so its Ambush succeeds; its legal retaliation can eliminate Yellow, who voted for Red. Red survives and Pink survives because Pink voted for a Target (Yellow). Yellow is eliminated. The status of any other players is unsupported because their votes and Ambush choices are not given.
answers.evidence: Vote: 'Ambush cards do not count as votes'; tied leaders 'are Targets.' Ambush: a successful ambusher 'survives and chooses one of the players who voted for them to eliminate.' Vote: with tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.

answers.answer: No. They eliminate only one of the four voters, not all four. They may not choose someone who voted for another color; the chosen player must have voted for the ambusher.
answers.evidence: Ambush: the successful ambusher chooses 'one of the players who voted for them'; 'They cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.'

answers.answer: That player eliminates themselves because an Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails.
answers.evidence: Ambush: 'An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.'

answers.answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, the game continues with another Conspire and vote among those surviving players only.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'Three or more | Continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.' Resolve the entire vote, including Ambush effects, before counting survivors and deciding whether to continue or award the pot.

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. These are four cards, not four points; each card has a value of 3, 4, or 5 points.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'One | That survivor collects all four central Gold Bars.' Components: 'Gold Bars are cards, not points' and their values are 3, 4, or 5 points.

answers.answer: They resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go. They may discuss intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card face down; when both are ready, they reveal simultaneously and resolve the pairing using the table.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: 'each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go'; each chooses one face down and, when both are ready, they reveal 'simultaneously.'

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar for this outcome. Nobody collects the four central bars; leave them for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: with none surviving, 'Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave the four central bars for the next round; add no new bars.' Special Rules: final voters receive no consolation bar.

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Share: 'You get 2; opponent gets 2.'

answers.answer: The Share player receives zero central bars and the Steal player receives all four central bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Steal: 'You get 0; opponent gets 4.'

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one central bar and the Steal player receives three central bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go versus Steal: 'You get 1; opponent gets 3.'

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one central bar and the Share player receives three central bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Grab One & Go: Share player gets 3 and Grab One & Go player gets 1.

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one central bar. Two bars remain in the center. If play continues, add just two new central bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: if both choose Grab One & Go, 'each finalist receives one central bar. Leave the remaining two in the center and add just two new bars for the next round.'

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: if both choose Steal, 'neither finalist receives gold'; 'give every other player one Gold Bar from the deck'; leave all four central bars and add no new gold.

answers.answer: Victory is checked at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded, regardless of how the round ended. With 6–9 players, the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players, it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: 'Check for victory at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded'; thresholds are 25 for 6–9 players and 24 for 10–12; 'the highest point total wins.'

answers.answer: If exactly two qualifying players tie for the highest Gold point total, the tied players conduct another Final Showdown. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including players eliminated earlier in that round; stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: 'If those totals are tied, the tied players conduct another Final Showdown.' Turn Structure: 'If there is no winner, everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.'
